items.title: vision_analyze fails with MiniMax — OpenAI image_url format sent to Anthropic-compatible endpoint
items.body:
## Bug Description

`vision_analyze` reports "no image attached" when `auxiliary.vision` is configured for the `minimax` provider (MiniMax-M2.7), even though the image URL is valid and downloadable.

## Root Cause

MiniMax's Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`/anthropic/v1/messages`) expects Anthropic's native **image content block format**:

```json
{"type": "image", "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": "image/png", "data": "..."}}
```

But `tools/vision_tools.py` sends images in **OpenAI `image_url` format**:

```json
{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,..."}}
```

The MiniMax endpoint receives the OpenAI format, cannot parse it as a vision image, and the model responds "no image attached."

## Configuration

```yaml
auxiliary:
  vision:
    provider: minimax
    model: MiniMax-M2.7
```

## Expected Behavior

`vision_analyze` should either:

1. Detect the provider and transform the content blocks to the provider's native format, OR
2. Document that MiniMax vision is unsupported and fall back to a provider that works (e.g. OpenRouter with a vision-capable model)

## Affected Files

- `tools/vision_tools.py` — `vision_analyze_tool` constructs messages with OpenAI-format `image_url` blocks regardless of target provider

items.title: Authorization layer for Hermes Agent — IBA Intent Bound Authorization
items.body:
## Authorization layer for Hermes Agent — IBA Intent Bound Authorization

### The Gap

Hermes Agent is the most compelling open-source agent framework of 2026. The learning loop, persistent memory, autonomous skill creation, and unattended cron scheduling are genuinely powerful.

They also describe the authorization gap precisely.

**"Natural language cron scheduling for reports, backups, and briefings — running unattended."**

What was the agent authorized to do while running unattended?
To what payees? Up to what spend limit? Under whose declared human intent?
What is the kill threshold if it exceeds scope?

Natural language declares intent. It does not enforce it.
A prompt can be overridden. A cryptographic certificate cannot.

---

### The Specific Scenarios

**Autonomous skill creation**
> "Autonomous skill creation after complex tasks. Skills self-improve during use."

The agent modifies its own capability set without a cert governing what it may modify. This is exactly the hyperagent authorization problem — once compounding starts, retrofitting bounds becomes impossible.

**Subagent delegation**
> "Isolated subagents with their own conversations, terminals, and Python RPC scripts."

Child agents operating with no parent certificate. No declared scope. No depth limit. No kill threshold on what the subagent may do that the parent was not authorized to do.

**Unattended execution**
> "Running unattended through the gateway."

60+ hours of autonomous operation with no declared human intent boundary. The Polymarket bot scenario. Made money this time. The gate was never there.

**Self-improving skills**
> "Skills self-improve during use."

An agent that modifies its own governance cannot be governed by what it modifies. The gate has to exist outside the learning loop — not inside it.

---

### The IBA Layer

IBA Intent Bound Authorization adds the missing primitive upstream of Hermes.

```json
{
  "intent": "Run weekly backup and audit report",
  "principal": "user@example.com",
  "scope": ["file_read", "report_write", "backup_execute"],
  "forbidden": ["payment", "external_api", "skill_modify", "subagent_spawn"],
  "limits": {
    "duration_hours": 8,
    "kill_threshold": "any_payment_attempt · any_skill_modification"
  },
  "issued": "2026-04-10T22:00:00Z",
  "expires": "2026-04-11T06:00:00Z",
  "signature": "ed25519:..."
}
```

**Gate logic:**
```
Certificate valid?                → PROCEED
Action outside declared scope?    → BLOCK
Skill modification attempted?     → BLOCK (kill threshold)
Subagent spawned without shard?   → BLOCK
Kill threshold triggered?         → TERMINATE + LOG
No certificate present?           → BLOCK
```

**No cert = No execution.**

The agent cannot modify skills it was not authorized to modify.
The subagent cannot exceed the parent certificate.
The cron job cannot act outside declared scope during unattended operation.
The learning loop cannot remove the gate that governs it.

---

### Shard Token Delegation for Subagents

```
Master Certificate (Human signed)
    │
    ├── Shard: SubAgent-1
    │     scope: [file_read, report_write]
    │     limit: 2 hours
    │     no_spawn: true
    │
    └── Shard: SubAgent-2
          scope: [backup_execute]
          limit: 1 hour
          no_spawn: true
```

No shard can exceed the parent.
No subagent operates without delegated authorization.
No trust in the subagent. Just enforced bounds.

Grok (xAI) Session 17: *"No trust in the sub-agent, just enforced bounds. Sub-1ms shard validation is exactly the scaling win we need for swarms."*

---

### Why Every Defense Inside the Loop Fails

PIArena tested 153 live platforms for prompt injection resistance. Every defense tested failed.

All of them operated inside the model's reasoning loop. The malicious instruction and the safety instruction are both text. The model interprets both.

IBA operates outside the loop entirely. The certificate is not text. It is not a prompt. It is not a skill file. It is a cryptographic boundary signed before the agent connects. It cannot be injected, overridden, or reasoned around.

---

### Patent & Standards Record

```
Patent:   GB2603013.0 (Pending) · UK IPO · Filed February 10, 2026
PCT:      150+ countries · Protected until August 2028
IETF:     draft-williams-intent-token-00 · CONFIRMED LIVE
          datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-williams-intent-token/
NIST:     13 filings
NCCoE:    10 filings · AI Agent Identity & Authorization
```

Priority date February 10, 2026 — before Hermes Agent's first release (February 25, 2026).

---

### Live Demos

**ibacore.com/swarm-html/** — Five-agent swarm with shard token delegation. Six violation scenarios including unauthorized spawn and scope breach.

**governinglayer.com/selfimprove-html/** — Agent self-improvement authorization. An agent cannot remove the gate that governs it.

**ibacore.com/desktopwars-html/** — Three desktop agents governed simultaneously under one IBA gate.

---

### Complementary, Not Competing

IBA does not replace Hermes Agent's architecture. It sits upstream of it.

Hermes provides the harness, the memory, the skill loop, the gateway.
IBA provides the pre-execution authorization boundary that makes unattended operation safe to deploy at scale.

The certificate is signed before the cron job fires. Hermes runs inside the declared envelope. The learning loop improves the agent. The gate governs what it is permitted to improve.

items.title: Context-length lookup misses openai-codex provider mapping (falls back to 128k)
items.body:
## Summary
When Hermes runs with `provider: openai-codex`, context-length resolution does not map that provider to models.dev's `openai` catalog.

As a result, models like `gpt-5.4-mini` can miss provider-aware metadata and fall back to the generic default (`128000`), which then causes premature compaction behavior (for example, `64k threshold (50%)`) and repeated session compression warnings.

## Repro
1. Configure Hermes with:
   - `model.provider: openai-codex`
   - `model.default: gpt-5.4-mini`
2. Resolve model context length through `get_model_context_length("gpt-5.4-mini", provider="openai-codex")`.

## Actual
Returns fallback-sized context (`128000`) in this path when provider-aware lookup misses.

## Expected
Should resolve through models.dev `openai` provider entry (e.g. `gpt-5.4-mini` => `400000`), avoiding premature compaction.

## Root cause
`PROVIDER_TO_MODELS_DEV` did not include:
- `openai -> openai`
- `openai-codex -> openai`

## Proposed fix
Add both mappings in `agent/models_dev.py` and add tests that assert:
- provider mapping contains `openai-codex`
- `get_model_context_length(..., provider="openai-codex")` uses models.dev provider-aware result.

## Why this matters
Incorrectly small context windows degrade long-running sessions and trigger avoidable compression cycles, especially for high-context GPT-5 variants.

## Problem

Telegram's `send_message` generates a link preview (og:image card) for the first URL in any message. There's no way to disable this from the agent/cron side.

This is noticeable when sending curated link lists (e.g., a weekly paper brief with 5 URLs) — only the first link gets a large preview card, making the message look unbalanced.

## Where

`gateway/platforms/telegram.py` — all `send_message` calls (lines ~840, ~852, ~1038, ~1103, ~1163).

None pass `link_preview_options`, so Telegram defaults to showing a preview for the first URL.

## Suggested fix

Add a config option under `telegram:` in `config.yaml`:

```yaml
telegram:
  link_preview: false  # default: true
```

Then in the gateway, when `link_preview` is false:

```python
from telegram import LinkPreviewOptions

kwargs["link_preview_options"] = LinkPreviewOptions(is_disabled=True)
```

python-telegram-bot already supports `LinkPreviewOptions` — just needs to be wired through.

## Bonus: per-message control

For more granular control, the agent could include a hint like `<!-- no-preview -->` in its response, and the gateway could detect it and disable preview for that message only. This would let cron prompts opt out without a global config change.

## Bug Description
When Feishu/Lark gateway is configured, the gateway process can crash on startup with a `NameError` because `gateway/run.py` uses `RedactingFormatter` but does not import it.

In my local environment this caused the launch agent to repeatedly restart and made it look like Feishu was "configured but not receiving messages".

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure Hermes gateway with Feishu/Lark enabled.
2. Start or restart the gateway service.
3. Observe the gateway crash during startup.
4. Check `~/.hermes/logs/gateway.error.log`.

## Expected Behavior
Gateway should start successfully and keep running.

## Actual Behavior
Gateway exits immediately with a `NameError`.

Example stack symptom:
```python
NameError: name 'RedactingFormatter' is not defined
```

Relevant code path:
- `gateway/run.py` sets:
  ```python
  _stderr_handler.setFormatter(RedactingFormatter('%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s'))
  ```
- but `RedactingFormatter` was not imported.

## Local Fix
Importing the formatter from `agent.redact` fixed the crash for me:
```python
from agent.redact import RedactingFormatter
```

After adding that import, the gateway started correctly again.

## Environment
- OS: macOS
- Repo: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Messaging platform: Feishu / Lark

## Notes
After fixing the missing import, I also hit a separate environment-specific issue where Lark websocket traffic under a SOCKS proxy required `python-socks`. Installing that dependency fixed my proxied setup, but the startup crash itself was caused by the missing `RedactingFormatter` import.

items.body:
## Description

When switching between custom providers using `hermes model`, the `api_mode` field in `config.yaml` is not updated to match the selected provider's `api_mode`. This causes API calls to fail silently or use the wrong protocol.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure two custom providers in `config.yaml`:
   - Provider A: `api_mode: anthropic_messages` (e.g. a Claude-compatible endpoint)
   - Provider B: `api_mode: openai` (e.g. local Ollama at `localhost:11434`)
2. Switch to Provider A via `hermes model` → works correctly
3. Switch to Provider B via `hermes model` → **`api_mode` remains `anthropic_messages`** instead of switching to `openai`

## Root Cause

In `_model_flow_named_custom()` ([main.py ~L1935](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/hermes_cli/main.py)), when activating a named custom provider, only `provider`, `base_url`, and `api_key` are written to the main `model` config. The `api_mode` from the selected `custom_providers` entry is ignored:

```python
model["provider"] = "custom"
model["base_url"] = base_url
if api_key:
    model["api_key"] = api_key
# ← api_mode is never set here
```

Each `custom_providers` entry already has an `api_mode` field — it just isn't being applied on switch.

## Expected Behavior

When switching to a named custom provider, `api_mode` in the main `model` config should be updated to match the `api_mode` defined in that provider's `custom_providers` entry.

## Suggested Fix

```python
api_mode = provider_info.get("api_mode")
if api_mode:
    model["api_mode"] = api_mode
else:
    model.pop("api_mode", None)  # let runtime auto-detect
```

## Environment

- macOS Darwin 25.3.0
- Providers affected: Ollama (openai mode) ↔ Anthropic-compatible endpoints (anthropic_messages mode)

items.title: Migration should not auto-archive source directory; needs coexistence guidance
items.body:
## Problem

`hermes claw migrate` automatically renames `~/.openclaw/` to `~/.openclaw.pre-migration/` in its Post-Migration Cleanup step — without separate confirmation.

### Code reference

In `hermes_cli/claw.py`:

- **Line 388-389**: Migration success unconditionally triggers `_offer_source_archival(source_dir, auto_yes)`
- **Line 428**: When `--yes` is passed, the archive executes without any prompt:
  ```python
  if auto_yes or prompt_yes_no(f"Archive {source_dir} now?", default=True):
      archive_path = _archive_directory(source_dir)  # rename
  ```

The `--yes` flag was approved by the user for "execute migration", but the archival of the source directory is silently bundled into the same flag. These are semantically different operations.

In interactive mode (tty), it does prompt `Archive ~/.openclaw now? [Y/n]` with default=Yes, which at least gives the user a choice. But `--yes` bypasses this entirely.

### Why this is problematic

1. **It assumes the user no longer needs OpenClaw.** Running both agents side-by-side is a valid use case (gradual transition, different models/providers, different workloads).
2. **The rename breaks OpenClaw** if the user intends to keep using it — OpenClaw expects `~/.openclaw/` to exist.

## Additional concern: coexistence conflicts

When both OpenClaw and Hermes run simultaneously on the same machine, shared resources can cause issues:

- **Channel conflicts (Telegram, Feishu, etc.):** If both agents are configured with the same bot token, they will fight over incoming messages — one receives the update, the other misses it, or both respond. This is a silent, confusing failure mode.
- **API key usage accounting:** Shared API keys (OpenRouter, Kimi, etc.) mean usage/billing is not separated per agent. Users may want distinct keys for cost tracking.

## Proposed behavior

### 1. Don't auto-archive — ask explicitly, with a separate flag

After migration completes, instead of bundling into `--yes`:

```
◆ Post-Migration Cleanup

  Keep the original ~/.openclaw/ directory?

  → Yes, keep it (I want to run both agents)
  → No, archive it to ~/.openclaw.pre-migration/
```

In non-interactive mode (`--yes`), **default to keeping** the source directory (safe default). Add a separate `--archive-source` flag for users who explicitly want the rename.

### 2. Coexistence guidance based on user's choice

**If the user chooses to keep OpenClaw**, display a prominent warning:

```
⚠ Coexistence Notice

  Both OpenClaw and Hermes are installed. To avoid conflicts:

  • Messaging channels (Telegram, Feishu, etc.): Do NOT use the same
    bot token in both agents — create a separate bot for Hermes, or
    stop OpenClaw's gateway before starting Hermes gateway.

  • API keys: Shared keys work but usage/billing won't be separated.
    Consider using distinct keys if you need per-agent cost tracking.
```

### 3. Skip channel token migration when coexisting

If the user indicates they want to keep OpenClaw running, the migration should **not** copy channel tokens by default (to prevent two agents polling the same bot). Instead, prompt:

```
  Telegram bot token found. Skip migration? (recommended if OpenClaw is still active)
  → Skip (I'll configure a new bot for Hermes)
  → Migrate anyway (I'll stop OpenClaw's gateway)
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.8.0 (2026.4.8)
- Affected file: `hermes_cli/claw.py` (lines 388-438)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Problem

`_patch_skill` in `tools/skill_manager_tool.py` line 429 crashes with:

```
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)
```

The destructuring `content, old_string, new_string, replace_all` expects 3 values but there are 4 variables on the left side — it looks like `replace_all` was added to the return/tuple but the unpacking wasn't updated.

## Impact

This is particularly bad for **cron jobs** — when a cron agent decides to save/update a skill post-response (standard SOUL.md behavior), the crash kills the session **before the response is delivered** to the target platform. The cron reports `last_status: ok` because the agent produced a response, but the user never sees it.

This means any cron that triggers the agent's "should I save a skill?" instinct silently drops its output.

## Repro

Any cron job where the agent tries to `skill_manage(action='patch', ...)` after producing its response.

Observed 4 consecutive times in gateway.log:

```
2026-04-12 01:28:33,337 ERROR tools.registry: Tool skill_manage dispatch error: too many values to unpack (expected 3)
  File "tools/skill_manager_tool.py", line 620, in skill_manage
  File "tools/skill_manager_tool.py", line 429, in _patch_skill
    content, old_string, new_string, replace_all
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)
```

## Fix

Line 429 in `_patch_skill` — update the tuple unpacking to match the number of values being returned/assigned.

items.title: Gateway process not cleaned up on unclean shutdown after provider timeout — bash/sleep children SIGKILL'd by systemd

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Describe the bug

When the Anthropic provider stops responding, the gateway logs a 180s timeout and attempts to reconnect. In the observed incident, tool calls (bash, sleep) continued to execute after the reconnect log message was emitted. When systemd eventually sent SIGTERM to the gateway process, it did not clean up its child processes within systemd's stop timeout, causing systemd to SIGKILL the remaining bash and sleep subprocesses.

**Note:** It is unclear whether the bash/sleep processes were spawned by the reconnect logic itself or were pre-existing subprocesses from active tool calls (terminal commands) running at the time of shutdown. This distinction matters for root cause — it may be a child process cleanup gap on shutdown rather than a reconnect-specific leak.

This has happened twice: once the previous evening (gateway died silently and was not discovered until the following morning), and once during an active session after the reconnect attempt.

Related: #4057 (missing timeouts on subprocess/network calls). Note also that #7503 (drain in-flight work before restart) was merged and addresses graceful shutdown on `/restart`, but the systemd SIGTERM path appears to still have this gap.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `hermes-gateway.service` under systemd as a **user service**
2. Have an active session with in-flight tool calls (e.g. bash/shell tool running)
3. Anthropic API becomes unresponsive for 180+ seconds during that session
4. Gateway logs: `No response from provider for 180s (model: claude-sonnet-4-6, context: ~614 tokens). Reconnecting...`
5. Tool calls continue to be dispatched after the above log line
6. Systemd issues SIGTERM to the gateway; gateway fails to exit cleanly within `TimeoutStopSec` (value not recorded — see notes)
7. Systemd escalates to SIGKILL on remaining child processes

**Note:** `TimeoutStopSec` for the `hermes-gateway.service` unit was not recorded during this incident. If a non-default value is relevant to reproduction, happy to check.

## Expected Behavior

On shutdown (SIGTERM), the gateway waits for in-flight tool calls to complete or forcibly terminates child subprocesses before exiting, so systemd receives a clean exit within `TimeoutStopSec`.

## Actual Behavior

From `journalctl` (05:37:48 UTC, gateway PID 28441):

```
hermes-gateway.service: Killing process 29771 (bash) with signal SIGKILL.
hermes-gateway.service: Killing process 29773 (sleep) with signal SIGKILL.
hermes-gateway.service: Consumed 27.724s CPU time.
```

Gateway did not restart automatically. Manual restart at 05:44:04 UTC started new instance (PID 29849).

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu
- Service type: systemd **user service** (not system-level)
- Trigger: Anthropic provider 180s timeout during active session with running tool calls
- TimeoutStopSec: unknown (not recorded during incident)
- Hermes-agent version: latest main
- Restart= in unit file: not configured (required manual restart)

items.body:
## Summary
The `/model` picker in the gateway/Telegram flow only shows a single model for `custom_providers` entries, even when the provider config contains multiple models under `custom_providers[].models`.

This appears to happen because the picker/listing path reads only `custom_providers[].model` and ignores `custom_providers[].models`.

## Sanitized example config
```yaml
model:
  default: model-a
  provider: custom
  base_url: https://redacted-gateway.example/v1

custom_providers:
  - name: Redacted Gateway
    base_url: https://redacted-gateway.example/v1
    model: model-a
    models:
      model-a: {}
      model-b: {}
      model-c: {}
      model-d: {}
```

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure a custom provider only under `custom_providers:` with one default model in `model:` / `custom_providers[].model` and several available models under `custom_providers[].models`.
2. Open `/model` in Telegram or another gateway surface that uses the interactive provider/model picker.
3. Select the custom provider.

## Expected behavior
The provider button should show the total number of configured models from `custom_providers[].models`, and the next picker step should list those configured models.

Using the sanitized example above, the provider should show `(4)` and the picker should offer `model-a`, `model-b`, `model-c`, and `model-d`.

## Actual behavior
The provider shows only `(1)`, and after selecting it the picker shows only the single value from `custom_providers[].model` (for example `model-a`).

## Suspected root cause
`hermes_cli/model_switch.py` `list_authenticated_providers()` currently builds the custom-provider model list from `entry.get("model")` only and does not consume `entry.get("models")`.

That means:
- `models_list` contains only one item
- `total_models` is reported as `1`
- the Telegram picker downstream receives only that single model

## Why this matters
This makes `/model` appear broken for custom OpenAI-compatible gateways that intentionally expose multiple models through a single endpoint.

It also creates a mismatch with other Hermes paths that already read richer metadata from `custom_providers`.

## Suggested fix
When building picker data for `custom_providers`, merge in model IDs from `custom_providers[].models`.

At minimum:
- if `entry["models"]` is a dict, use its keys as the available model IDs
- fall back to `entry["model"]` only when `entry["models"]` is absent or empty
- set `total_models` from the full model set, not just the default model

## Notes
This report uses a redacted provider name and redacted base URL. It does not include any user-private endpoint details.

items.title: [Bug]: Telegram duplicate replies when interrupted session sends stale response before processing pending message
items.body:
### Bug Description

When a new Telegram message arrives for an already-active session, Hermes marks the running session as interrupted and queues the new message in _pending_messages. However, the running task still sends its old response before checking whether it has been interrupted. After that, the queued message is processed and produces another response.

This causes duplicate or near-duplicate visible replies, especially when the two prompts are closely related.

Telegram flood control makes the symptom worse because the stale response may be delayed and arrive noticeably later, making it look like Hermes repeated itself.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a Telegram conversation with Hermes in a single DM or single session thread.
2. Send a prompt that takes some time to process, especially one likely to produce a long answer.
3. Before Hermes has fully finished sending the previous reply, send another related prompt in the same session.
4. Observe that Hermes may first send a stale reply from the earlier turn and then send a second reply for the newer turn.
5. Under Telegram flood control, the stale reply may arrive late, making the two responses look like duplicate answers.

### Expected Behavior

If a running session has been interrupted by a newer incoming message, the stale response from the older turn should not be sent. Hermes should suppress the old reply and continue with the queued newer message only.

### Actual Behavior

The interrupted older turn still sends its response, and then the queued newer message is processed and also sends a response. This creates duplicate or highly overlapping visible replies.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat) Kernel: Linux 6.17.0-1007-aws

### Python Version

Python 3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.8.0

### Relevant Logs / Traceback

```shell
Supporting Evidence From Logs

Observed in /home/ubuntu/.hermes/logs/agent.log for Telegram DM chat 5769327191:

- 06:42:57 inbound: Hermes Live 重复回答
- 06:43:09 response ready: 514 chars
- 06:44:08 Sending response (111 chars)
- 06:44:13 inbound again: Hermes Live 重复回答

Also earlier in the same DM session:

- 06:17:52 response ready: 2658 chars
- 06:19:36 new inbound arrives before the prior turn has fully cleared
- 06:22:06 another response ready: 2871 chars
- 06:29:16 another inbound arrives while the session is still busy

This matches the active-session interrupt path rather than duplicate execution by two gateway processes.

Flood Control Interaction

Telegram flood control is present in the same log window, e.g.:

- Telegram flood control on send (attempt 1/3), retrying in ...
- Telegram flood control, waiting ...

Flood control is not the primary bug, but it amplifies the user-visible symptom by delaying stale sends.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The interrupt path is incomplete:

- gateway/platforms/base.py:1507-1559
  - if a session is active, a new incoming message is stored in _pending_messages[session_key]
  - the interrupt flag is set via self._active_sessions[session_key].set()
- gateway/platforms/base.py:1628-1718
  - _process_message_background() awaits self._message_handler(event)
  - then immediately sends the response with _send_with_retry()
  - there is no check for interrupt_event.is_set() / pending replacement before sending
- gateway/platforms/base.py:1831-1845
  - only after sending does the code pop _pending_messages and process the queued event

So the stale response from the interrupted turn is still delivered, followed by the response for the newer turn.

Why this is the definitive cause

The current code path deterministically allows this sequence:

1. message A starts processing
2. message B arrives while the same session is active
3. B is queued and interrupt flag is set
4. A still sends its response
5. queued B is then processed and also sends a response

No duplicate gateway instance is required, and no duplicate inbound delivery is required.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Suggested Fix

In gateway/platforms/base.py, after response = await self._message_handler(event) and before any send call:

- check whether interrupt_event.is_set() or whether session_key in self._pending_messages
- if true, skip sending the stale response from the old turn
- proceed directly to the queued pending event

Possible patch shape:

response = await self._message_handler(event)

if interrupt_event.is_set() or session_key in self._pending_messages:
    logger.info("[%s] Suppressing stale response for interrupted session %s", self.name, session_key)
    response = None

A more careful version should distinguish true cancel/replacement from benign queued photo-burst behavior.

items.title: Discord image attachments fail with 403: use att.read() instead of plain HTTP download
items.body:
## Bug Description

When users send images in Discord, Hermes fails to analyze them because downloading Discord CDN attachment URLs via plain HTTP returns **403 Forbidden**.

## Root Cause

In `gateway/platforms/discord.py`, image attachments are downloaded using `cache_image_from_url(att.url)` which makes a plain `httpx` request without Discord authentication. Discord CDN attachment URLs increasingly require the bot session to download successfully.

Additionally, in `gateway/platforms/base.py`, any HTTP error with status code < 429 (including 403) is raised immediately without retry:
```python
if isinstance(exc, httpx.HTTPStatusError) and exc.response.status_code < 429:
    raise
```

This causes the code to fall back to the raw CDN URL, which also returns 403 when passed to the vision tool.

## Fix

Use `discord.Attachment.read()` (which uses the bot's authenticated session) instead of plain HTTP download:

```python
# In discord.py, replace:
cached_path = await cache_image_from_url(att.url, ext=ext)

# With:
try:
    image_bytes = await att.read()
    cached_path = cache_image_from_bytes(image_bytes, ext=ext)
except Exception:
    cached_path = await cache_image_from_url(att.url, ext=ext)
```

Same fix applies to audio attachments (`cache_audio_from_url` → `att.read()` + `cache_audio_from_bytes`).

`cache_image_from_bytes` already exists in `gateway/platforms/base.py` (line 95).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up Hermes with a Discord bot
2. Send an image attachment in Discord
3. Hermes replies it cannot see/analyze the image

## Expected Behavior

Hermes downloads the attachment via the bot session and successfully passes it to the vision tool for analysis.

## Environment

- Hermes v0.8.0
- macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Discord gateway

## Summary
The Telegram platform hint in `agent/prompt_builder.py` currently tells the model:

> Please do not use markdown as it does not render.

    "Please do not use markdown as it does not render. "

This can cause the agent to incorrectly avoid markdown structure on Telegram even when the user prefers it and the adapter supports conversion.

In practice it pushes responses toward worse formatting and can override user formatting preferences for no valid reason.

The Telegram platform hint should not claim markdown does not render.
It should instead say something like:

- markdown formatting is supported and converted for Telegram when needed, or
- simple formatting is fine, but markdown is supported via Telegram formatting conversion.

The repository root `package.json` and root `package-lock.json` are currently out of sync.

Specifically, `package.json` declares `@askjo/camoufox-browser`, but the checked-in root `package-lock.json` does not include that dependency tree.

items.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming messages show extra leading blank lines after edits
items.body:
### Bug Description


### Description

When Hermes streams a response to Feishu, the message gains extra leading blank lines during streaming. The initial message appears correctly, but as soon as the first streaming edit is applied, 1–2 blank lines appear above the text content. The issue persists for the rest of the stream and the message is marked "(已编辑)" in the Feishu client.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes with a Feishu bot (WebSocket or Webhook mode)
2. Better switch to  claude-haiku-4.5, coz he'd like to send lot's of "Perfect! ....." new message.
2. Send a prompt that triggers a long/streamed response (e.g. one requiring tool use or search)
3. Observe the message in the Feishu client while it is being streamed

### Expected Behavior

The message text begins at the top of the bubble with no leading blank lines, both on initial send and during streaming edits.
*(message is marked 已编辑)*

### Actual Behavior

After the first streaming edit, the message displays as:

```
(blank line)
(blank line)
Let me check the actual JIRA address...
```

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp), Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Operating System

Ubuntu 22.04

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.8.0

### Relevant Logs / Traceback

```shell
no
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`send()` calls `format_message()` which strips leading/trailing whitespace before building the outbound payload. `edit_message()` did not call `format_message()`, so it passed the raw LLM output (which commonly begins with `\n\n`) directly to `_build_outbound_payload()`. Feishu renders the leading `\n\n` as blank lines.

Additionally, `_clean_for_display()` in `stream_consumer.py` uses `.rstrip()` only, so leading newlines from the LLM stream are not removed before being passed to `edit_message()`.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Add `content = self.format_message(content)` in `edit_message()` before the payload is built, matching the existing behavior in `send()`.

items.title: hermes gateway restart returns before restart completes
items.body:
## Bug Description

hermes gateway restart returns immediately after requesting a restart, but the gateway process actually exits and does not automatically restart. The user must manually run hermes gateway start after every restart call.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. hermes gateway start — gateway is running
2. hermes gateway restart — returns '✓ User service restart requested' immediately
3. hermes gateway status — shows '✗ User gateway service is stopped'

## Expected Behavior

hermes gateway restart should block until the gateway is back up and running, similar to systemctl restart.

## Root Cause

In hermes_cli/gateway.py, the systemd_restart() function (line 1097):

```python
def systemd_restart(system: bool = False):
    ...
    pid = get_running_pid()
    if pid is not None and _request_gateway_self_restart(pid):
        print(f'✓ {_service_scope_label(system).capitalize()} service restart requested')
        return   # <-- returns immediately after SIGUSR1
    subprocess.run(_systemctl_cmd(system) + ['reload-or-restart', ...])
```

It sends SIGUSR1 to the gateway process (graceful drain-and-restart signal), prints the success message, then returns immediately without waiting for the gateway to actually restart.

The gateway then shuts down (drain), exits with code 75. The systemd unit has Restart=on-failure and RestartSec=30, so it does eventually restart — but after a 30-second delay, and the restart command already returned.

## Suggested Fix

systemd_restart() should wait for the service to become active again after requesting the restart, e.g.:

```python
# After sending SIGUSR1, poll status until active or timeout
import time
deadline = time.time() + 60
while time.time() < deadline:
    result = subprocess.run(
        _systemctl_cmd(system) + ['is-active', get_service_name()],
        capture_output=True, text=True
    )
    if result.stdout.strip() == 'active':
        print(f'✓ {_service_scope_label(system).capitalize()} service restarted')
        return
    time.sleep(1)
print('✗ Service restart timed out')
``"

items.title: Bug: symlinked skills under ~/.hermes/skills are omitted from skills_list and bare-name skill_view lookup

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

Directory symlink skills placed under `~/.hermes/skills/<category>/<name>` can be directly readable on disk, but Hermes discovery misses them in multiple places.

Observed behavior:
- `skills_list` omits the skill
- `skill_view("bare-name")` returns not found
- `skill_view("category/name")` can still work
- direct file reads like `~/.hermes/skills/social-media/follow-builders/SKILL.md` work fine

This creates a confusing partial-failure mode where the skill exists and is readable, but normal discovery and bare-name lookup behave as if it does not exist.

## Reproduction

1. Create a real skill directory outside Hermes, for example:
   - `~/skill_hub/follow-builders/SKILL.md`
2. Symlink it into the local skills tree:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/.hermes/skills/social-media
   ln -s ~/skill_hub/follow-builders ~/.hermes/skills/social-media/follow-builders
   ```
3. Confirm the target file is readable:
   ```bash
   test -f ~/.hermes/skills/social-media/follow-builders/SKILL.md && echo ok
   ```
4. In Hermes:
   - call `skills_list`
   - call `skill_view("follow-builders")`
   - call `skill_view("social-media/follow-builders")`

## Actual behavior

- `skills_list` does not include `follow-builders`
- `skill_view("follow-builders")` returns not found
- `skill_view("social-media/follow-builders")` succeeds

## Expected behavior

A skill symlinked into `~/.hermes/skills/...` should behave like a first-class local skill:
- it should appear in `skills_list`
- bare-name lookup should work when the name is unique
- discovery should be consistent with direct path loading

## Why this happens

There are at least two discovery paths that do not follow directory symlinks:

1. `tools/skills_tool.py`
   - `_find_all_skills()` scans with `scan_dir.rglob("SKILL.md")`
   - bare-name fallback in `skill_view()` also scans with `search_dir.rglob("SKILL.md")`

2. `agent/skill_utils.py`
   - `iter_skill_index_files()` uses `os.walk(skills_dir)` without `followlinks=True`

On Python 3.11+, these scans do not recurse into directory symlinks, so symlinked skills are skipped during recursive discovery even though direct path access still works.

## Symptom pattern

This is easy to miss because some code paths still succeed:
- direct path access to the symlinked directory works
- `skill_view("category/name")` can work because the direct-path branch checks `search_dir / name`
- but recursive scans miss the same skill

So the user sees an inconsistent system where the skill both exists and does not exist depending on the lookup path.

## Workaround

Using `skills.external_dirs` pointing at the real source directory works reliably. For example:

```yaml
skills:
  external_dirs:
    - /absolute/path/to/skill_hub
```

After switching to `external_dirs`, the same skill becomes discoverable via `skills_list` and `skill_view("follow-builders")`.

## Possible fixes

A few possible approaches:

1. Make recursive discovery explicitly follow directory symlinks where appropriate
   - for `os.walk`, use `followlinks=True`
   - for `rglob`, replace with a traversal that follows symlinked directories intentionally

2. Centralize skill discovery so list/view/prompt-builder/gateway all share one traversal implementation

3. Preserve safety by following only symlinks that remain within trusted skill roots, or document the intended policy clearly if symlinked local skills are unsupported

## Related issue

This seems adjacent to, but distinct from, #4759.

#4759 is about `skill_manage` not handling `external_dirs` consistently.

This issue is about ordinary local discovery under `~/.hermes/skills/` failing when the skill directory itself is a symlink.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent main branch as of 2026-04-12
- Python 3.11
- macOS

items.title: [Bug]: Prompt caching is not enabled for custom Anthropic-compatible providers using api_mode: anthropic_messages
items.body:
## Bug Description

Prompt caching is not auto-enabled for third-party Anthropic-compatible providers that use `api_mode: anthropic_messages`, even when the endpoint supports Anthropic `cache_control` and the selected model is Claude.

One concrete example is ZenMux's Anthropic-compatible endpoint:

```yaml
custom_providers:
  zenmux-anthropic:
    base_url: https://zenmux.ai/api/anthropic
    api_key: ${ZENMUX_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}
    api_mode: anthropic_messages
    models:
      anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5:
        context_length: 200000
      anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6:
        context_length: 400000
      anthropic/claude-opus-4.6:
        context_length: 400000
```

With this provider selected in Hermes, prompt caching is not activated.

## Expected Behavior

If the runtime is using `api_mode: anthropic_messages` and the endpoint is Anthropic-compatible, Hermes should be able to enable Anthropic prompt caching for Claude models, or at least offer a way to opt into it for compatible providers.

In this configuration, Hermes should send Anthropic cache breakpoints / `cache_control` markers the same way it does for native Anthropic.

## Actual Behavior

Hermes does not enable prompt caching for the configuration above.

From the current `main` branch, the gating logic appears to be provider-name based instead of capability based:

```python
# run_agent.py
is_openrouter = self._is_openrouter_url()
is_claude = "claude" in self.model.lower()
is_native_anthropic = self.api_mode == "anthropic_messages" and self.provider == "anthropic"
self._use_prompt_caching = (is_openrouter and is_claude) or is_native_anthropic
```

The same pattern appears again in model-switch / fallback re-evaluation paths.

This means any named custom provider using `api_mode: anthropic_messages` is excluded from prompt caching unless the provider name is literally `anthropic`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a custom provider like the ZenMux example above.
2. Select a Claude model from that provider.
3. Start a Hermes session and send a few multi-turn prompts.
4. Observe that prompt caching is not enabled for this provider path.

## Why this seems like a Hermes-side issue

ZenMux documents Anthropic prompt caching support on its Anthropic-compatible endpoint and shows `cache_control` being sent to `https://zenmux.ai/api/anthropic`.

So the issue seems less about the endpoint lacking support, and more about Hermes never turning on the cache-marker path for third-party `anthropic_messages` providers.

## Suggested Direction

The enabling condition probably needs to move from provider-name matching to capability matching.

For example, something along these lines:

- `api_mode == anthropic_messages`
- model is Claude
- endpoint is native Anthropic or a compatible `/anthropic` endpoint, or the provider explicitly declares prompt-cache support

Even an explicit provider-level opt-in would solve this cleanly.

## Version / Context

Observed on current Hermes configuration with a custom provider using `api_mode: anthropic_messages`.

If helpful, I can open a PR for the gating change after the expected behavior is agreed.

items.title: Feishu outbound audio upload omits duration, causing incorrect/0s duration display
items.body:
## Bug description
When Hermes sends an outbound audio message to Feishu/Lark, the message can play normally but may show an incorrect duration (for example `0s`).

In local testing, the problem appears specifically on the upload step for outbound audio files: the Feishu SDK upload body supports a `duration` field, but Hermes does not currently pass it when uploading audio before sending the `audio` message.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure Hermes with a working Feishu/Lark gateway.
2. Generate or provide an outbound audio file (for example `.ogg` / `.opus`).
3. Send it through the Feishu adapter as an outbound audio message.
4. Observe the message in Feishu.

## Expected behavior
The outbound audio message should display the correct duration metadata in Feishu/Lark.

## Actual behavior
The audio can be playable, but the duration metadata may be missing or displayed incorrectly (for example `0s`).

## Root cause
In `gateway/platforms/feishu.py`, outbound audio upload currently builds `CreateFileRequestBody` with fields like:
- `file_type`
- `file_name`
- `file`

But the Feishu SDK also supports `duration` on `CreateFileRequestBody` for audio uploads.

In local verification:
- manually uploading the same audio with `duration=<milliseconds>` made Feishu return/send the audio message with the correct duration
- patching Hermes locally to probe audio duration and pass it into the upload body also worked

## Suggested fix
When the resolved outbound message type is `audio`:
1. probe the local audio duration in milliseconds
2. pass `duration` into `CreateFileRequestBody`
3. upload the file as usual, then send the `audio` message with the returned `file_key`

A minimal local patch in `gateway/platforms/feishu.py` was enough to fix this in testing.

## Environment
- Hermes repo: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Platform: Feishu/Lark
- OS tested: Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL

If helpful, I can open a follow-up PR with the small Feishu adapter fix.

items.title: Weixin streaming exposes partial message and punctuation-only continuation when editing is unsupported
items.body:
## Summary

When token streaming is enabled on Weixin, the gateway can expose a partial assistant message with the streaming cursor (`▉`) and then follow it with a second message that starts with punctuation such as `，`.

Example user-visible output:

- `我是 Hermes ▉`
- `，你可以把我当成一个助手。`

## Root cause

`GatewayStreamConsumer` assumes progressive message editing is available during streaming.

`WeixinAdapter` inherits the default `BasePlatformAdapter.edit_message()` implementation, which returns `success=False, error="Not supported"`.

That allows this failure mode:

1. a partial message is sent with the streaming cursor
2. a follow-up edit is attempted
3. editing is unsupported on the platform
4. fallback delivery sends only the unsent tail
5. the user sees a cursor-stuck partial plus a punctuation-leading continuation

## Expected behavior

For platforms that do not support message editing, partial streamed text should not be exposed.

Instead, the gateway should wait until the final response is complete and send a single clean message.

## Reproduction

Use `GatewayStreamConsumer` with a `WeixinAdapter` and stream:

- `我是 Hermes`
- `，你可以把我当成一个助手。`

Before the fix, the visible output becomes:

- `我是 Hermes ▉`
- `，你可以把我当成一个助手。`

## Proposed fix

Detect adapters that do not implement real `edit_message()` support, and suppress visible partial streaming for them until the final response is complete.

## Validation

- Added a regression test covering the Weixin / non-editable-platform case
- Verified:
  - `tests/gateway/test_stream_consumer.py`
  - `tests/gateway/test_weixin.py`

items.title: [Feishu]: Tool call results displayed as separate messages instead of single card
items.body:
## Description

When Hermes executes multiple tool calls in sequence (e.g. `read_file`, `web_search`, `terminal`), each tool's result is displayed as a separate message bubble or card in the Feishu client, rather than being accumulated into a single updating card.

This creates a cluttered chat experience where a single user query can generate 5-10+ separate tool progress messages, each appearing as a distinct card.

## Expected Behavior

All tool progress updates should be edited into a single message/card (similar to how Telegram streaming works). The user should see one card that progressively updates with each tool result, not N separate cards.

## Actual Behavior

Each tool call result appears to produce a separate message in Feishu. Possible causes:

1. `edit_message()` fails silently for Feishu, causing fallback to `send()` (new message each time)
2. CardKit streaming card updates may not properly accumulate tool results
3. The `send_progress_messages()` logic in `gateway/run.py` (lines ~7479-7574) correctly edits the same message, but Feishu's `edit_message` implementation may not preserve message position or may trigger re-renders

## Environment

- hermes version: v0.8.0
- Feishu connection mode: WebSocket
- OS: Linux Ubuntu

## Related

- #7675 (streaming card support for Feishu)
- #8252 (blank lines in streaming edits - fixed by #8310)

items.body:
### Bug Description

# Bug: (regression) `display.streaming` Enables Gateway Message Streaming Despite `streaming.enabled: false`

## Summary

Gateway message streaming to messaging platforms (eg. Discord) is enabled when `display.streaming: true` is set, even if the root gateway streaming config has `streaming.enabled: false`.

This contradicts the documentation, where `display.streaming` is described as CLI/terminal token streaming and root-level `streaming.enabled` controls progressive message editing in messaging platforms.`

## Fun fact

This is the reason why so many streaming issues are being opened right now. Because streaming got suddenly enabled for a lot of people.


### Steps to Reproduce


With the config set to:

```yaml
display:
  streaming: true

streaming:
  enabled: false
```

Messages are STILL streamed to messaging platforms which contradicts the documentation.

### Expected Behavior

With root gateway streaming disabled:

```yaml
streaming:
  enabled: false
```

Messaging platforms should NOT receive progressively edited streamed messages unless they have platform specific overrides.

Root `display.streaming: true` should only affect the CLI terminal streaming display as per the docs.

### Actual Behavior

Discord receives streamed/edited messages anyway.

Observed behavior:

- Messages are sent with a streaming cursor and then edited into the final text.
- Discord displays the messages as edited.

In a focused reproduction on latest `upstream/main`, delayed stream chunks produced:

```text
sent: ['interim status', 'first streamed chunk ▉']
edits: ['first streamed chunk plus final chunk']
```

That happened with root `streaming.enabled: false`.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Operating System

Gateway running on Linux

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.8.0

### Relevant Logs / Traceback

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Latest `upstream/main` at the time of investigation:

```text
45e60904 fix: fall back to provider's default model when model config is empty (#8303)
```

The gateway resolves effective streaming using:

```python
_plat_streaming = resolve_display_setting(user_config, platform_key, "streaming")

_streaming_enabled = (
    _scfg.enabled and _scfg.transport != "off"
    if _plat_streaming is None
    else bool(_plat_streaming)
)
```

`resolve_display_setting(..., "streaming")` checks global `display.streaming`, not just `display.platforms.<platform>.streaming`. Therefore this config:

```yaml
display:
  streaming: true
streaming:
  enabled: false
```

resolves `_plat_streaming` to `True`, which overrides root gateway streaming being disabled.

items.body:
## Bug Description
When attempting to send files (PDF, documents) via the Weixin adapter, the operation fails with a 404 Not Found error from the CDN upload endpoint.

## Environment
- **Hermes Version**: 0.8.0
- **Platform**: Weixin (WeChat) via iLink Bot API
- **OS**: Linux (Docker container)
- **Python**: 3.13.5

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure Weixin adapter with valid credentials
2. Start Hermes Gateway: `hermes gateway run`
3. Attempt to send a PDF file via Weixin using `adapter.send_document()`

## Expected Behavior
File should be uploaded to WeChat CDN and sent successfully to the recipient.

## Actual Behavior
The operation fails with HTTP 404 error:

```
ERROR gateway.platforms.weixin: [Weixin] send_document failed: 
404, message='Not Found', 
url='https://novac2c.cdn.weixin.qq.com/c2c/upload?encrypted_query_param=...'
```

## Error Details
The error occurs in `_upload_ciphertext()` function when attempting to POST encrypted file data to the CDN URL obtained from `getUploadUrl` API.

**Stack trace location:**
- File: `hermes/gateway/platforms/weixin.py`
- Function: `_upload_ciphertext()` (line ~506)
- Called from: `_send_file()` (line ~1536)

## Analysis
The issue appears to be related to:
1. **CDN endpoint change**: The URL `novac2c.cdn.weixin.qq.com` may have been deprecated or changed by Tencent
2. **API version incompatibility**: iLink Bot API may have updated their CDN upload mechanism
3. **Upload parameter format**: The `upload_param` returned by `getUploadUrl` may need different encoding/processing

## Related Code
```python
# _cdn_upload_url function (line ~301-306)
def _cdn_upload_url(cdn_base_url: str, upload_param: str, filekey: str) -> str:
    return (
        f"{cdn_base_url.rstrip('/')}/upload"
        f"?encrypted_query_param={quote(upload_param, safe='')}"
        f"&filekey={quote(filekey, safe='')}"
    )
```

## Impact
**High**: File sending functionality is completely broken for Weixin adapter. Users cannot send PDFs, documents, or any file attachments via WeChat.

## Additional Context
- Text messages work correctly
- The issue started recently (was working in previous versions)
- Tencent may have updated their iLink API without backward compatibility

## Possible Solutions
1. Update CDN base URL to the new endpoint
2. Change upload mechanism to use `upload_full_url` instead of `upload_param` when available
3. Implement fallback to alternative upload methods

## References
- [Weixin Adapter Documentation](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/messaging/weixin)

---

**Suggested Labels**: `bug`, `platform:weixin`, `priority:high`, `media-upload`

items.body:
## Bug Description

When a dangerous command triggers an approval card in Feishu, the card displays 4 buttons:
- ✅ Allow Once (primary/highlighted by default)
- ✅ Session
- ✅ Always
- ❌ Deny

**Expected behavior:** When the user clicks a button other than "Allow Once", the card should immediately update to visually reflect the user's selection (e.g., highlight the clicked button, dim others, or show a spinner).

**Actual behavior:** The card remains unchanged after clicking — the "Allow Once" button stays highlighted. Only after the backend processes the approval does the card get replaced with a final resolved status card.

This creates a confusing UX where users are unsure if their click was registered.

## Root Cause

In `gateway/platforms/feishu.py`, the `send_exec_approval()` method creates the card with only the initial state:

```python
_btn("✅ Allow Once", "approve_once", "primary"),  # 'primary' makes this highlighted
_btn("✅ Session", "approve_session"),               # default type
_btn("✅ Always", "approve_always"),                  # default type
_btn("❌ Deny", "deny", "danger"),                   # danger type
```

When a button is clicked, `_handle_card_action_event` calls `resolve_gateway_approval()` and then `_update_approval_card()` to replace the card — but this replacement happens **after** backend processing, not **during** the button click itself.

There is no intermediate state update (e.g., optimistic UI update showing the clicked button as selected).

## Suggested Fix

Two options:

### Option A: Immediate card update on click (recommended)
1. When a button is clicked, immediately update the card to show selected state
2. Then process the approval in background
3. Finally replace with resolved card

This would require adding an `UPDATE_APPROVAL_CARD` method or using Feishu's message update API to change button styles immediately.

### Option B: Use Feishu button interaction updates
Feishu interactive cards support `value` updates on button click. The card could be designed to:
1. Show a "processing..." state on the clicked button
2. Use Feishu's built-in card refresh mechanism

## Environment
- Platform: Feishu
- Hermes version: current
- Python package: nousresearch/hermes-agent

## Related Code
- `gateway/platforms/feishu.py` lines 1401-1498
- `send_exec_approval()` — creates the card
- `_handle_card_action_event()` — handles button clicks
- `_update_approval_card()` — updates to final state

## Repro Steps
1. Trigger a dangerous command approval in Feishu
2. Observe the card with highlighted "Allow Once" button
3. Click any other button (e.g., "Deny")
4. Observe: no visual change to the card until after backend processing completes

items.body:
## Summary

An automated documentation audit noticed several places where the docs/specs appear to describe behavior that may no longer match the current implementation, as well as a few implementation details that seem undocumented or hardcoded. A number of these may simply reflect design docs becoming stale as the code evolved, so we wanted to report them in one place for review.

> **Note:** This issue was generated automatically by [LyingDocs](https://github.com/KMing-L/lying-docs), a documentation-code misalignment detection tool. The analysis may contain errors or misinterpretations — please feel free to close or correct this issue if any finding does not apply or if we have misunderstood the codebase.

## Finding Categories

The findings below are classified into one or more of the following categories:

| Category | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| **LogicMismatch** | The code behaves differently from what the documentation describes |
| **PhantomSpec** | The documentation describes a feature or behavior that does not appear to exist in the code |
| **ShadowLogic** | The code contains significant behavior that is not documented at all |
| **HardcodedDrift** | A value or parameter described as configurable in the docs is hardcoded in the implementation |

## Findings

### ACP streaming behavior appears different from setup docs

- **Category**: LogicMismatch
- **Documentation reference**: `acp-setup.md:198-201`
- **Code reference**: `acp_adapter/server.py:394`

The ACP setup docs say ACP streams responses incrementally, but it appears that the ACP server currently wires thinking/tool progress callbacks and returns assistant text only as a final response. We noticed that `AIAgent` seems to support streaming text via `stream_delta_callback` / `interim_assistant_callback`, but ACP does not appear to connect those paths. If intentional, the docs may need to clarify what is streamed versus what is only emitted at completion.

### ACP log level env var may be documented but not honored

- **Category**: LogicMismatch
- **Documentation reference**: `acp-setup.md:216-220`
- **Code reference**: `acp_adapter/entry.py:23`

The docs suggest `HERMES_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG hermes acp` enables verbose ACP logging. From the audited entrypoint, it seems logging is hardcoded to INFO and does not consult `HERMES_LOG_LEVEL`. It may be worth clarifying whether env-based log verbosity is still supported.

### Documented `HERMES_MODEL` override may no longer exist

- **Category**: PhantomSpec
- **Documentation reference**: `acp-setup.md:158-166`
- **Code reference**: `cli.py:1644`

The setup docs say users can change the model through the `HERMES_MODEL` environment variable. We could not find support for that override in the current code, and it appears `config.yaml` is treated as authoritative. If that env var was removed, the docs may need updating.

### Pricing plan may understate existing cost-status support

- **Category**: LogicMismatch
- **Documentation reference**: `plans/2026-03-16-pricing-accuracy-architecture-design.md:29-30`
- **Code reference**: `agent/usage_pricing.py:15`

The plan states that the current system has no distinction between live estimates and reconciled billed cost. However, it appears the code already defines `CostStatus` values such as `actual`, `estimated`, `included`, and `unknown`, and persists related status/source fields. It seems the missing piece may be actual reconciliation flow rather than the status model itself.

### Pricing plan's description of current token storage may be stale

- **Category**: LogicMismatch
- **Documentation reference**: `plans/2026-03-16-pricing-accuracy-architecture-design.md:25-30`
- **Code reference**: `run_agent.py:1356`

The plan describes the current system as storing only prompt/completion token totals. In the current code, it appears there are already more detailed token buckets such as `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, and `reasoning_tokens`, along with billing metadata.

### Pricing plan's CLI current-state section appears outdated

- **Category**: LogicMismatch
- **Documentation reference**: `plans/2026-03-16-pricing-accuracy-architecture-design.md:460-468`
- **Code reference**: `cli.py:6314`

The plan says `cli.py` currently computes session cost directly from prompt/completion totals. The audited `/usage` flow appears to build a `CanonicalUsage` from input/output/cache buckets and render a `CostResult` with status and source metadata instead.

### Reconciliation architecture appears only partially implemented

- **Category**: PhantomSpec
- **Documentation reference**: `plans/2026-03-16-pricing-accuracy-architecture-design.md:374-383`
- **Code reference**: `run_agent.py:8549`

The design discusses authoritative post-hoc provider reconciliation, but we could not find the runtime flow that writes `actual_cost_usd`, sets status to `actual`, or stores reconciliation IDs in the audited path. It seems possible that the code contains schema/types anticipating this future state, while the live reconciliation behavior described in the plan is not yet implemented.

### Honcho integration spec may describe an older initialization model

- **Category**: LogicMismatch
- **Documentation reference**: `honcho-integration-spec.md:19-22`
- **Code reference**: `run_agent.py:1148`

The Honcho spec describes Honcho as being initialized directly in `AIAgent.__init__` without a plugin boundary. In the current implementation, it appears `AIAgent` initializes a generic memory manager and loads Honcho through the memory-provider plugin system (`plugins.memory.honcho`).

### Honcho spec references method names that may not exist

- **Category**: PhantomSpec
- **Documentation reference**: `honcho-integration-spec.md:25-34`
- **Code reference**: `agent/memory_manager.py:167`

The spec names `_honcho_prefetch()` and `_honcho_fire_prefetch()` as Hermes methods. We could not find those methods in the current code; the implementation appears to use provider-agnostic methods such as `prefetch_all()` and `queue_prefetch_all()` instead.

### Honcho per-peer memory mode schema may be undocumented in code

- **Category**: PhantomSpec
- **Documentation reference**: `honcho-integration-spec.md:173-205`
- **Code reference**: `plugins/memory/honcho/client.py:187`

The spec documents config keys like `memoryMode`, `userMemoryMode`, and `agentMemoryMode` with precedence rules. These keys do not appear to be implemented in current Honcho config parsing, which seems to use different settings such as `recallMode`, `writeFrequency`, `dialecticReasoningLevel`, `sessionStrategy`, `sessionPeerPrefix`, and `sessions`.

### Honcho session strategy docs may not match resolver behavior

- **Category**: LogicMismatch
- **Documentation reference**: `honcho-integration-spec.md:271-307`
- **Code reference**: `plugins/memory/honcho/client.py:420`

The spec describes session naming strategies as `per-directory`, `global`, manual map, and title-based, with a particular fallback order. The current code appears to support additional strategies such as `per-session` and `per-repo`, and the fallback behavior seems to differ as well. We also were not sure whether title-based naming is fully wired from `AIAgent` initialization, so this one may especially benefit from maintainer clarification.

### Honcho CLI command names and mode values appear to have drifted

- **Category**: LogicMismatch
- **Documentation reference**: `honcho-integration-spec.md:262-267`
- **Code reference**: `plugins/memory/honcho/cli.py:1242`

The spec documents commands as bare `honcho ...` and says `mode` accepts `hybrid|honcho|local`. The current CLI surface appears to be `hermes honcho ...`, with `setup` delegating to `hermes memory setup`, and `mode` choices of `hybrid|context|tools`.

### Honcho prompt injection described in spec may not be implemented

- **Category**: PhantomSpec
- **Documentation reference**: `honcho-integration-spec.md:310-330`
- **Code reference**: `plugins/memory/honcho/__init__.py:370`

The spec says Hermes injects a compact Honcho management-command reference into the system prompt when Honcho is active. In the current prompt block, we only noticed mode/tool guidance and optional context, not a command cheat-sheet or management-command reference.

### Honcho spec may be missing additional implemented strategies and commands

- **Category**: ShadowLogic
- **Documentation reference**: `honcho-integration-spec.md:271-307`
- **Code reference**: `plugins/memory/honcho/client.py:454`

It appears the implementation supports additional session strategies (`per-session`, `per-repo`) and a broader CLI surface (`peer`, `peers`, `tokens`, `migrate`, `enable`, `disable`, `sync`, `identity --show`) that are not covered in the integration spec.

### Container exec flow may still wrap probe failures

- **Category**: LogicMismatch
- **Documentation reference**: `specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md:29-33`
- **Code reference**: `hermes_cli/main.py:543`

The container CLI spec says `_exec_in_container` is “completely transparent” and that `subprocess.run` remains only for the sudo probe. In the current implementation, it appears both direct and sudo inspect probes are wrapped in `_probe_container()`, with custom timeout/probe-failure messages and `sys.exit(1)` on several paths.

### Malformed `.container-mode` behavior may be more tolerant than spec says

- **Category**: LogicMismatch
- **Documentation reference**: `specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md:41-43`
- **Code reference**: `hermes_cli/config.py:188`

The spec says malformed `.container-mode` data should “LET IT CRASH”. The current implementation appears to let unreadable file errors propagate, but malformed content itself is mostly tolerated: non-`key=value` lines are ignored and missing fields seem to fall back to defaults such as `backend='docker'` and `container_name='hermes-agent'`.

### Container CLI spec test count appears stale

- **Category**: LogicMismatch
- **Documentation reference**: `specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md:289`
- **Code reference**: `tests/hermes_cli/test_container_aware_cli.py:1`

A minor one: the spec says the existing container-aware CLI test file has 16 tests, but the current file appears to contain 18 test functions. This may just be a stale count in the document.

### Container probe timeout is fixed at 15 seconds

- **Category**: HardcodedDrift
- **Documentation reference**: `specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md:77-78`
- **Code reference**: `hermes_cli/main.py:549`

The spec references a 15-second container probe timeout, and the implementation appears to hardcode that exact value in `_probe_container()`. If that value is intentionally fixed, the docs might say so explicitly; otherwise it may be worth deciding whether it should be configurable.

## Suggested follow-up

- Review whether the affected docs/specs should be updated to reflect current behavior, especially for ACP setup, Honcho integration, and container CLI behavior.
- For the pricing architecture plan, consider marking sections as historical/current-state snapshots versus future design goals, if that is the intent.
- If some documented behaviors are still intended, consider updating the implementation to restore them (for example, ACP text streaming or env-controlled ACP log level).
- If any of these findings are based on incomplete context or audited the wrong runtime path, a quick clarification in comments would be very helpful, and feel free to close the issue.

---
*If any of the above findings are false positives or we have misunderstood the context, we sincerely apologize for the noise. Please close this issue or leave a comment and we will take note.*

items.body:
## Feature Request

### Problem
The Slack adapter hardcodes 👀 (eyes) and ✅ (white_check_mark) reactions on every processed message (`slack.py` lines 1138-1145). There is no configuration option to disable this behavior.

Discord and Telegram adapters both support a `reactions` config toggle:
- `discord.reactions: true/false` → mapped to `DISCORD_REACTIONS` env var
- `telegram.reactions: true/false` → mapped to `TELEGRAM_REACTIONS` env var

But Slack has no equivalent. The `slack` section in `config.yaml` only supports `require_mention` and `free_response_channels`.

### Use Case
When the bot monitors channels via `free_response_channels`, it receives **all** messages but should only react/respond selectively. Currently it adds 👀 to every single message, which is noisy and reveals that the bot is processing messages users did not explicitly direct at it.

### Proposed Solution
Add a `reactions` toggle to the Slack config, consistent with Discord and Telegram:

```yaml
slack:
  require_mention: false

items.title: [Bug]: Flood control causes duplicate streaming replies (already_sent flag not set on interrupt)
items.body:
### Bug Description

When Telegram flood control (rate limiting) interrupts the streaming progress of a message, the system sends the full response again as a separate message, causing a duplicate reply with identical content.

This differs from the interrupt-race condition (#8221) where two different responses are sent. In this bug, the same content is delivered twice due to incorrect already_sent flag handling.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Send a prompt to Hermes that generates a long streaming response
2. Either:
   - Send multiple messages in rapid succession to trigger flood control
   - Or have the bot generate a very long response that hits rate limits
3. Observe that the response appears twice:
   - First message: partial content (streaming was interrupted)
   - Second message: complete text (full response resent)

### Expected Behavior

The response should appear exactly once, even if streaming was interrupted by flood control. If partial content was already delivered, the full response should not be sent again.

### Actual Behavior

The user receives the same response twice:
1. First via progressive streaming edits (partial, then interrupted)
2. Second as a complete message (duplicate)


### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS

### Python Version

Python 3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.8.0

### Relevant Logs / Traceback

```shell
Log pattern showing the bug:
# Stream consumer sends partial content
Telegram flood control on send (attempt 1/3), retrying in ...

# Later, gateway sends full response again
Sending response (514 chars) to ... response_id=abc send_batch_id=xyz


Key observation: Two messages with different send_batch_id values but same content.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Location: gateway/run.py, lines 8401-8411 (in _run_agent method)

Old (buggy) logic:
_sc = stream_consumer_holder[0]
if _sc and isinstance(response, dict) and not response.get("failed"):
    _response_previewed = bool(response.get("response_previewed"))
    if (
        getattr(_sc, "final_response_sent", False)
        or (
            _response_previewed          # ← PROBLEM: Required True
            and getattr(_sc, "already_sent", False)
        )
    ):
        response["already_sent"] = True

Why it fails:

When flood control interrupts the final edit:
- final_response_sent = False (final edit blocked by flood control)
- already_sent = True (partial content was successfully sent earlier)
- response_previewed = False (not set in this code path)

The condition response_previewed and already_sent evaluates to False, so already_sent flag is NOT set on the response.

In base.py _process_message_background, since already_sent is not set, the gateway sends another copy of the complete response.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Simplify the condition to match the queued message handling logic:

_sc = stream_consumer_holder[0]
if _sc and isinstance(response, dict) and not response.get("failed"):
    # Fix: if streaming has sent ANY content (already_sent=True),
    # don't send the full response again — even if streaming was
    # interrupted by flood control and didn't set final_response_sent.
    if (
        getattr(_sc, "final_response_sent", False)
        or getattr(_sc, "already_sent", False)
    ):
        response["already_sent"] = True


Files Modified:
- gateway/run.py (lines 8401-8411)

Test Matrix:

| Scenario | final_response_sent | already_sent | response_previewed | Before Fix | After Fix |
|----------|-------------------|--------------|-------------------|------------|-----------|
| Normal completion | True | True | True | ✓ | ✓ |
| Flood interrupt (BUG) | False | True | False | ✗ duplicate | ✓ fixed |
| No content sent | False | False | True | ✓ | ✓ |

items.title: Slack: assistant.threads.setStatus persists after response when MCP tools execute post-reply
items.body:
## Description

When using Slack's Assistant API with MCP servers configured, the "Evaluating..." / "is thinking..." typing indicator persists after Casey (the bot) has already sent its text response. The indicator eventually auto-clears after Slack's ~2 minute timeout, but the UX is confusing — users see the response AND an active typing indicator simultaneously.

## Root Cause

In `gateway/platforms/slack.py`, `send_typing()` (line 341) calls `assistant.threads.setStatus("is thinking...")` at the start of processing. Slack's docs state the status "auto-clears when the bot sends a reply."

However, when MCP tool calls (e.g., MemPalace) execute **after** the main text response is sent, Slack appears to detect continued activity and keeps the indicator alive. The status is never explicitly cleared with `setStatus(status="")`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an MCP server (e.g., MemPalace) in `mcp_servers` config
2. Enable Slack assistant events (`assistant_thread_started`, `assistant_thread_context_changed`)
3. Send a message that triggers both a text response AND post-response MCP tool calls
4. Observe: response appears, but "Evaluating..." persists for ~2 minutes after

## Expected Behavior

The typing indicator should clear immediately after the final response is sent, regardless of background MCP tool execution.

## Suggested Fix

Add an explicit `assistant.threads.setStatus(status="")` call after the response is fully delivered and any synchronous post-response processing completes. In the stream consumer or gateway runner, after the final message is sent:

```python
await self._get_client(chat_id).assistant_threads_setStatus(
    channel_id=chat_id,
    thread_ts=thread_ts,
    status="",  # Explicitly clear
)
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: latest (installed 2026-04-12 via install.sh)
- Platform: Slack (Socket Mode)
- MCP Server: MemPalace v3.1.0 (stdio transport)
- Memory Provider: Hindsight (local_embedded)
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04, DigitalOcean s-2vcpu-4gb
- Slack scopes include `assistant:write`

## Workaround

The indicator auto-clears after ~2 minutes (Slack's built-in timeout). Removing `assistant_thread_started` and `assistant_thread_context_changed` from event subscriptions eliminates the assistant UI entirely but loses suggested prompts and thread context features.

items.body:
---

`[SECURITY] WhatsApp self-chat mode responds to ALL incoming messages (empty allowlist = allow everyone)`

```
## Security Issue

**Severity:** Medium-High
**Component:** WhatsApp Bridge

### Description
In `self-chat` mode (default), the bridge processes messages from ANY sender. Anyone who messages the user triggers a Hermes response.

### Root Cause
Two issues compound:

1. **`allowlist.js` line 67-68** — Empty allowlist returns `true`:
```javascript
if (!allowedUsers || allowedUsers.size === 0) {
  return true; // ← everyone allowed!
}
```

2. **`bridge.js` line 231** — No mode distinction for non-`fromMe` messages:
```javascript
if (!msg.key.fromMe && !matchesAllowedUser(senderId, ALLOWED_USERS, SESSION_DIR)) {
  continue;
}
```

`WHATSAPP_ALLOWED_USERS` defaults to empty → everyone passes.

### Impact
Any person messaging the user gets a pairing code reply. Affects ALL users without explicit allowlist config.

### Fix
In `bridge.js`, add mode-aware filtering:
```javascript
if (!msg.key.fromMe) {
  if (WHATSAPP_MODE === 'self-chat') {
    continue; // Self-chat: never respond to other people
  }
  if (!matchesAllowedUser(senderId, ALLOWED_USERS, SESSION_DIR)) {
    continue;
  }
}
```

And in `allowlist.js`, change empty allowlist default to `return false`.
```

---

For the PR, fork it, create a branch, apply those two changes, and submit. Want me to prepare the exact diff you can paste?

## Feature: Integrate with Archon CLI for deterministic workflow orchestration

**Labels**: `feature-request`, `integration`, `high-priority`

---

### Problem
Hermes Agent lacks deterministic workflow orchestration capabilities (DAG-based execution, isolation, per-node model selection, database persistence). This limits production use cases requiring repeatable, auditable multi-step operations.

**Current strengths:**
- ✅ Hook system for AI agent control
- ✅ Flexible model providers (OpenRouter, Ollama, Anthropic, OpenAI)
- ✅ Skills system (SKILL.md files)
- ✅ Platform adapters (Telegram, Discord, Slack)

**What's missing:**
- ❌ No workflow engine (no DAG, no node-based execution)
- ❌ No isolation (single session, no parallel-safe environments)
- ❌ No per-node model selection (one model per session)
- ❌ No database-backed workflow state (session-only)
- ❌ No loop gates with deterministic conditions
- ❌ No workflow resume/skip completed nodes

---

### Solution
Integrate with Archon CLI as a workflow orchestration backend, while preserving Hermes's AI agent flexibility.

**Value proposition:**
- ✅ **Preserve existing workflow** - Keep using Hermes's flexible AI, skills, hooks
- ✅ **Add deterministic orchestration** - Leverage Archon's battle-tested DAG engine (16.7k GitHub users)
- ✅ **Per-node model selection** - Smart LLM for planning, cheap/local for execution
- ✅ **Parallel-safe isolation** - Git worktrees prevent conflicts between concurrent operations
- ✅ **Database persistence** - Workflows resume after interruption, skip completed nodes
- ✅ **Minimal coupling** - Hermes calls Archon as subprocess, no shared state needed

**What I wish Hermes to implement:**

1. **CLI integration layer**
   - Add `archon_integration.py` module for subprocess execution
   - CLI flags: `--archon-workflow <name>`, `--archon-list`, `--archon-status <run-id>`

2. **SSE streaming integration (optional but recommended)**
   - Capture Archon's Server-Sent Events for real-time progress updates

**Why this matters:**

- ✅ **For Hermes Agent users:** Adds production-grade workflow orchestration without rebuilding core
- ✅ **Leverages Archon's mature code and battle-tested features**
- ✅ **Enables deterministic, repeatable operations**
- ✅ **Per-node model switching** for cost optimization

**Many thanks!**
