items.title: [Bug]: pip install -e .[all] hangs indefinitely on Raspberry Pi 3B / 32-bit ARM — faster-whisper has no armv7l wheels

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug Description

Installing Hermes Agent on a Raspberry Pi 3B — either via `scripts/install.sh` or via `hermes update` on an existing install — hangs indefinitely. The process sits in `pip install -e .[all]` for hours trying to build `ctranslate2` and `onnxruntime` from source. These are transitive dependencies of `faster-whisper`, which is pulled in via the `voice` optional-extras group, referenced unconditionally from `[all]`.

On 1GB-RAM devices the source build either OOMs, fills the 128MB `/tmp` tmpfs, or never finishes in any reasonable timeframe. Because `hermes update --gateway` runs `pip install` as a child of the running gateway, the Telegram `/update` command never returns and the bot becomes unresponsive until the stuck pip process is killed manually. The stale `.update_pending.json` state file then causes every subsequent gateway restart to replay the unfinished update output to Telegram until the state files are cleaned up by hand.

This is functionally equivalent to the Termux case already documented in the `termux` optional-extras group, whose comment explicitly calls out `faster-whisper -> ctranslate2` as the reason that group avoids `[voice]`. The Raspberry Pi 3B / 2 / Zero class of 32-bit ARM Linux hosts suffer the same issue but have no automatic handling.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Provision a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B Rev 1.2 with Raspbian Bookworm 12 (32-bit, `armv7l`), 1GB RAM, Python 3.11.2.
2. Install hermes-agent via `scripts/install.sh` (which detects `armv7l` and installs Node.js, so the platform is nominally supported).
3. Run `hermes update` from the CLI, OR send `/update` to an already-running Telegram gateway.
4. Observe: the process reaches `→ Updating Python dependencies...` and hangs.
5. `ps auxf` shows `pip install -e .[all] --quiet` consuming ~85% CPU in the `R` state for hours; `df -h /tmp` climbs toward 100%.

## Expected Behavior

`pip install -e .[all]` should complete successfully on 32-bit ARM Linux hosts, installing every extras group that has prebuilt wheels. `voice`-related functionality (local STT via faster-whisper) should be skipped automatically on those hosts — mirroring the existing `termux` extras' rationale — and remain available as a manual opt-in via `pip install -e '.[voice]'` for users who really need it.

## Actual Behavior

`pip install -e .[all]` never finishes. It spends hours attempting to build `ctranslate2` and `onnxruntime` from source because no `armv6l` / `armv7l` wheels are published on PyPI for either package. A user hitting this via the Telegram `/update` command sees a silent gateway hang, and `.update_pending.json` keeps replaying the stale output on every restart.

## Affected Component

- Setup / Installation

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

- Telegram

(Root cause is install-layer, not Telegram-specific — any user running `hermes update` or `pip install -e .[all]` on `armv7l` will hit it.)

## Operating System

Raspbian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm), 32-bit; kernel `6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v7`

## Python Version

3.11.2

## Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.8.0 (2026.4.8)

## Relevant Logs / Traceback

```shell
$ /data/apps/hermes/venv/bin/python3 -m pip install -e .[all] --quiet
# (hangs here indefinitely — no output)

$ ps auxf | grep -E "hermes|pip install"
aras  21455 ... python3 -m hermes_cli.main gateway
aras   1369 ... bash -c "... /usr/local/bin/hermes update --gateway ..."
aras   1370 ...   \_ python3 -m hermes_cli.main update --gateway
aras   1403 ...      \_ python3 -m pip install -e .[all] --quiet   (76% CPU, R state)

$ df -h /tmp
tmpfs   128M   110M    19M   86%   /tmp

$ uname -m
armv7l

$ cat /proc/device-tree/model
Raspberry Pi 3 Model B Rev 1.2
```

## Root Cause Analysis

The issue is in `pyproject.toml`. The `[all]` meta-extra aggregates `hermes-agent[voice]` unconditionally (line 106 on current `main`):

```toml
all = [
  ...
  "hermes-agent[voice]",
  ...
]
```

`voice` defines `faster-whisper >= 1.0.0`, which transitively depends on `ctranslate2` and `onnxruntime`. Neither package publishes 32-bit ARM wheels to PyPI (only `aarch64`, `x86_64`, `arm64`, etc.), so pip falls back to building them from source, which on a 1GB-RAM Pi 3B either OOMs or runs indefinitely with `/tmp` filling up.

The `voice` extras definition already flags the risk in a comment:

```toml
voice = [
  # Local STT pulls in wheel-only transitive deps (ctranslate2, onnxruntime),
  # so keep it out of the base install for source-build packagers like Homebrew.
  "faster-whisper>=1.0.0,<2",
  ...
]
```

…and the `termux` extras documents the same problem as its reason for existing:

```toml
termux = [
  # Tested Android / Termux path: keeps the core CLI feature-rich while
  # avoiding extras that currently depend on non-Android wheels (notably
  # faster-whisper -> ctranslate2 via the voice extra).
  ...
]
```

But there is no automatic handling for 32-bit ARM Linux hosts like the Raspberry Pi 3B class — they hit the same failure without any guardrail.

## Proposed Fix

Gate the `voice` entry in `[all]` with a `platform_machine` environment marker, mirroring the existing `[matrix]; sys_platform == 'linux'` pattern merged in #7461:

```toml
all = [
  ...
  "hermes-agent[voice] ; platform_machine != 'armv6l' and platform_machine != 'armv7l'",
  ...
]
```

This keeps the default `pip install -e .[all]` path working on `x86_64`, `arm64`, `aarch64`, and every other architecture exactly as before, but transparently skips `voice` (and therefore `faster-whisper -> ctranslate2 -> onnxruntime`) on 32-bit ARM. Users who genuinely need local STT on an ARM32 host can still install it explicitly:

```bash
pip install -e '.[voice]'
```

I have a PR ready implementing this fix plus a regression test in `tests/test_packaging_metadata.py`.

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

`gateway.log` is not attached on the normal `hermes gateway run` startup path because logging is initialized in CLI mode first, and the later gateway-mode initialization is skipped by the global idempotency guard.

## Affected version

Observed on commit `4eecaf06`.

## Reproduction

1. Start Hermes through the normal CLI entrypoint:
   ```bash
   hermes gateway run
   ```
2. Generate some gateway activity.
3. Inspect `~/.hermes/logs/`.

## Actual behavior

- `agent.log` and `errors.log` are active.
- `gateway.log` exists but remains empty, or is never attached as an active handler.
- Gateway logger output still lands in `agent.log`.

## Expected behavior

`gateway.log` should be attached and should receive records from `gateway.*` loggers during `hermes gateway run`.

## Root cause

The CLI entrypoint initializes logging in CLI mode very early:

- `hermes_cli/main.py` calls `setup_logging(mode="cli")`

Later, gateway startup tries to initialize gateway logging:

- `gateway/run.py` calls `setup_logging(..., mode="gateway")`

But `hermes_logging.setup_logging()` returns early once `_logging_initialized` is already `True`, so the gateway-specific handler is never added.

That means the code path that creates the filtered `gateway.log` handler is skipped on the normal CLI -> gateway startup flow.

## Minimal reproduction at the Python level

```python
import hermes_logging

hermes_logging.setup_logging(mode="cli")
hermes_logging.setup_logging(mode="gateway")
```

Result: only `agent.log` and `errors.log` are attached.

If `setup_logging(mode="gateway")` is called first, `gateway.log` is created correctly.

## Suggested fix

When `setup_logging()` is called again with `mode="gateway"`, it should still ensure that the `gateway.log` handler exists instead of returning immediately.

One approach would be:

- keep the function idempotent for existing handlers
- but on a later `mode="gateway"` call, add the missing `gateway.log` handler if it has not been attached yet

## Regression test suggestion

Add a test that covers this exact sequence:

1. `setup_logging(mode="cli")`
2. `setup_logging(mode="gateway")`
3. assert that `gateway.log` handler exists and receives `gateway.*` records

items.title: [Feature]: Support namespaced skill names (e.g. superpowers:writing-plans) to avoid name collisions
items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Hermes currently uses a flat skill naming system — each skill is identified solely by its name field in the [SKILL.md](http://skill.md/) frontmatter. This creates problems when installing third-party skill collections like [obra/superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers), which contains 14 skills that may share names with existing Hermes skills.

### Proposed Solution

**For example**, if a user already has a systematic-debugging skill installed and then installs the superpowers collection, the two skills overwrite each other — there's no way for both to coexist.
How other platforms handle this

### Claude Code

Claude Code supports namespaced skill invocation via the `superpowers`: prefix:

```
Skill("superpowers:writing-plans")
Skill("superpowers:systematic-debugging")
Skill("superpowers:subagent-driven-development")
```
When the superpowers plugin is installed, Claude Code's plugin infrastructure automatically:

1. Registers skills with their `superpowers:` namespace prefix
2. Routes `Skill("superpowers:xxx") `calls to the correct skill file
3. Allows coexistence with user-installed skills of the same base name

### OpenCode
OpenCode also supports namespaced skill names, but has hit edge cases when the prefix is missing. Their [PR #981](https://github.com/obra/superpowers/pull/981) discusses:

- Skills without `superpowers:` prefix trigger `"Did you mean?"` warnings
- The framework expects fully qualified names for cross-skill references
- They're working on a bootstrap convention to enforce prefix consistency

superpowers internal cross-references
The superpowers collection itself uses namespaced references internally:
This shows that namespacing is the expected pattern for multi-source skill ecosystems.

### Alternatives Considered

### Comparison Summary
**Proposed Solution**
Add support for namespaced skill names using : as a separator (matching Claude Code's convention):

1. Skill loading: Skills from a subdirectory or plugin source should be registered with a namespace prefix, e.g. superpowers:writing-plans
2. Skill invocation: Agent should be able to call skill_view("superpowers:brainstorming") or equivalent
3. Skill listing: skills_list() should show namespaced names clearly
4. Backward compatibility: Non-namespaced skills (flat names) continue to work as before

**Example directory layout**

```
~/.hermes/skills/
├── systematic-debugging/        # user-installed, called as "systematic-debugging"
├── superpowers/                  # plugin directory
│   ├── systematic-debugging/    # superpowers version, called as "superpowers:systematic-debugging"
│   ├── writing-plans/           # called as "superpowers:writing-plans"
│   └── subagent-driven-development/
```

### Why this matters

- Ecosystem growth: As more skill collections become available (superpowers, custom enterprise skills, etc.), name collisions are inevitable
- User choice: Users should be able to keep their existing skills while also trying new collections
- Cross-platform compatibility: Skills written for Claude Code already use superpowers: prefix in their internal references — supporting this makes migration easier
- No breaking change: Flat skill names can coexist with namespaced ones

### Alternatives considered

- Rename on install (e.g. sp-systematic-debugging): Breaks internal cross-references that use superpowers: prefix
- Priority/override system: Loses the overwritten skill entirely, no way to use both
- Manual merge: High maintenance burden, defeats the purpose of composable skills

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

items.title: Agent triggers repeated gateway restarts due to lack of self-restart awareness (hallucination loop)
items.body:
## Bug Description

When Hermes executes `systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway` via the terminal tool,
it has **no way to detect that the restart actually happened**. This leads to a destructive
hallucination loop where the agent continuously restarts the gateway without user consent.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask Hermes to configure a model that requires gateway restart
2. Hermes decides to restart the gateway (sometimes without asking user consent first)
3. Hermes executes `systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway` via terminal tool
4. Gateway restarts successfully
5. User asks: "Did you restart?"
6. Hermes says "No, I didn't restart" — because it genuinely has no memory of the restart
7. User says "Please restart the gateway"
8. Hermes restarts the gateway again
9. Repeat steps 5-8 in a loop

## Root Cause

Hermes has **zero self-awareness** about gateway restarts it triggered:

- The terminal tool executes the command and returns stdout/stderr
- Hermes sees "command executed successfully" but cannot observe the side effect
- After the gateway restarts, Hermes itself is restarted
- When session resumes, Hermes only has conversation history — **no restart event record**
- The agent genuinely doesn't know it already restarted

## Comparison with OpenClaw

OpenClaw can detect self-triggered restarts:
1. Records the command it executed
2. Compares gateway PID before the command
3. Compares gateway PID after the command
4. If PID changed, knows it triggered the restart

Hermes lacks this mechanism entirely.

## Impact

- **User consent bypass**: Agent restarts gateway without asking (sometimes)
- **Hallucination loop**: Agent doesn't know it restarted, continues to restart on user request
- **User frustration**: User watches agent restart gateway repeatedly without understanding why
- **Broken trust**: Agent appears to "lie" about not restarting, but it's genuinely unaware

## Expected Behavior

Hermes should be able to:
1. Detect when it has triggered a gateway restart
2. Be aware of this event in subsequent conversation context
3. Not restart the gateway again if it already restarted
4. Ideally: Ask for user confirmation before any gateway restart

## Suggested Fix

Options (from least to most complex):

1. **Self-restart awareness**: After executing `systemctl restart`, the agent checks if the gateway PID changed. If so, it logs "I triggered a gateway restart" to session context.

2. **Restart detection hook**: When gateway restarts, inject a system message into the session: `[System: Gateway restarted at HH:MM:SS]`

3. **Terminal tool enhancement**: The terminal tool should report PID changes when executing systemctl commands that affect the gateway process.

4. **Approval gate**: Any `systemctl restart` command should require user approval before execution, not after.

This is a serious UX failure that makes the agent appear incompetent and untrustworthy.

items.title: [Bug]: smart_model_routing silently overrides session-scoped /model switch for simple messages

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

When `smart_model_routing` is enabled and a user has explicitly switched model/provider via the `/model` command, short or simple messages (e.g. `hi`, `thanks`, `yes`) are silently rerouted to the configured cheap model instead of the user's chosen model.

The root cause is that `resolve_turn_route()` in `agent/smart_model_routing.py` has no awareness of session-scoped `/model` overrides. It unconditionally evaluates the cheap-model heuristic on every turn and can replace the session-overridden model.

This is a gap left after PR #7662, which correctly wired session overrides into agent construction but did not guard the smart routing layer.

## Steps to Reproduce

### Config

```yaml
# ~/.hermes/config.yaml
model:
  default: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6
  provider: openrouter

smart_model_routing:
  enabled: true
  max_simple_chars: 160
  max_simple_words: 28
  cheap_model:
    provider: openrouter
    model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
```

### Reproduction

1. Start a chat session: `hermes chat`
2. Switch model explicitly: `/model gpt-5.4 --provider openai-codex`
3. Confirm the switch is acknowledged
4. Send a short message: `hi`

### Expected Behavior

The request is sent to `gpt-5.4` on `openai-codex` — the model the user explicitly chose.

### Actual Behavior

The request is silently sent to `openai/gpt-4o-mini` on `openrouter` — the configured cheap model from `smart_model_routing`. The user's `/model` override is ignored for this turn.

Sending a longer or more complex message (e.g. containing keywords like "debug", "implement", etc.) correctly falls through smart routing and uses the session-overridden model, making the behavior inconsistent and confusing.

## Root Cause Analysis

Call chain on current `main`:

1. `/model gpt-5.4 --provider openai-codex` stores the override in `_session_model_overrides[session_key]` → `gateway/run.py:4396`
2. Next message arrives → `_resolve_session_agent_runtime()` correctly reads the override and returns `model="gpt-5.4"`, `runtime_kwargs={provider: "openai-codex", ...}` → `gateway/run.py:860-876`
3. `_resolve_turn_agent_config()` packages model + runtime into `primary` dict and calls `resolve_turn_route(user_message, routing_config, primary)` → `gateway/run.py:879-893`
4. **Bug**: `resolve_turn_route()` unconditionally calls `choose_cheap_model_route(user_message, routing_config)` → `smart_model_routing.py:115`
5. For short, simple messages, `choose_cheap_model_route()` returns a route with the cheap model → `smart_model_routing.py:103-107`
6. `resolve_turn_route()` returns `route.get("model")` (the cheap model) instead of `primary.get("model")` (the session override) → `smart_model_routing.py:176`

**Key observation**: `resolve_turn_route()` receives no information about whether `primary` came from a session override or from global config defaults. It treats both identically.

### Affected code paths

All three call sites that invoke `_resolve_turn_agent_config()` are affected:

| Call site | Location | session_key available? |
|---|---|---|
| `_run_agent()` | `gateway/run.py:7619` | Yes (parameter) |
| `_run_background_task()` | `gateway/run.py:5234` | Derivable from `source` |
| `_run_btw_task()` | `gateway/run.py:5400` | Yes (parameter) |

## Affected Component

- Gateway (model routing)
- Agent Core (smart_model_routing module)

## Impact

- Users who rely on `/model` to switch providers mid-session will have their choice silently ignored for simple messages
- Particularly affects users who switch to a specific model for a series of quick questions
- Can cause unexpected billing if the cheap model routes to a different provider with different pricing
- Related to #7798: when smart routing replaces the model, it also triggers preflight compression against the cheap model's smaller context window

## Hermes Version

v0.8.0+ (post-PR #7662 merge on 2026-04-11)

## Proposed Fix

PR #8459 — adds a `session_override_active` keyword argument to `resolve_turn_route()` that skips cheap-model routing when a `/model` session override is active.

## Related Issues

- #7662 (closed) — fixed session overrides for agent construction paths, but missed the smart routing layer
- #7798 (open) — smart routing triggers preflight compression against cheap model threshold; this issue is a prerequisite — if smart routing doesn't override the model, the compression threshold bug doesn't trigger for session-overridden models
- #4568 (open) — CLI status bar shows stale model during smart routing (same category of smart-routing-mutates-state bugs)

items.body:
## Problem

The root `hermes` CLI parser does not accept `-m/--model` or `--provider` flags. This means users cannot specify a model or provider when launching Hermes from the command line, forcing them to rely on config defaults or in-session /model switching.

## Expected Behavior

```bash
hermes chat -m anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
hermes chat --model openai/gpt-4o --provider openrouter
hermes gateway -m qwen/qwen3.6-plus
```

## Implementation

Add `-m/--model` and `--provider` arguments to the root argument parser in `hermes_cli/main.py`, alongside existing global flags like `-v/--verbose` and `-Q/--quiet`. These should propagate through to the `chat` and `gateway` subcommands.

## Motivation

Consistency with common CLI conventions for model selection and aligns with the /model picker functionality already available in-session.
